customManagers.description: Home Assistant add-on base images pinned in Dockerfile FROM/ARG lines and the HA image tag pinned in the dep-proxy e2e docker-compose.yml. A single manager across both file types so a bump moves every reference together in one PR (the alternative — separate per-file managers or the built-in dockerfile manager for FROM + inline ``# renovate:`` annotations for the rest — split the bumps and stranded one set when the other merged).

Upstream Signal K server base image pinned in the signalk Dockerfile (ARG BUILD_FROM default) -- the single source for the base version (the add-on has no build.yaml; the e2e and CI build from this default). It lives on docker.io, so it falls outside the ghcr.io/home-assistant manager above and needs its own matcher to stay current.

Pinned halpid (HALPI2 power controller daemon) release built from source in the halpi2_power Dockerfile. Upstream tags are v<semver>+<rev>; regex versioning so the +<rev> packaging bumps compare too. The add-on's watchdog patch is pinned against a specific release, so a bump that stops the patch applying fails the build loudly -- the intended review signal.
GitHub runner versions in shell scripts and YAML within workflows
Renovate npm package version pinned in CI workflows
Pinned ffmpeg apt package in the integration-test workflow

APK packages pinned in Alpine 3.24 Dockerfiles. Version lookups go through a custom datasource that reads Alpine's own APKINDEX for the pinned suites and returns a Renovate-shaped release list. Replaces the previous Repology datasource (see #6).

home-assistant/builder build-image action (calver-tagged sub-path). Versioning is explicitly 'loose' so the calver tags (2026.06.0) compare correctly — the helpers:pinGitHubActionDigestsToSemver preset would otherwise apply semver to this depName globally, which silently ignores calver and surfaces the old pre-calver semver tags (4.x, 7.x) as 'latest' (cf. closed PRs #246 / #248).
frenck/action-addon-linter schema URLs in pre-commit config

npm packages pinned via pre-commit additional_dependencies (e.g. @commitlint/config-conventional@N in .pre-commit-config.yaml). The built-in pre-commit manager only bumps the `rev:` on each hook — it doesn't touch the additional_dependencies array. Standardized permissive form matches both @scoped and unscoped packages across all sibling repos.
uv tool required-version pin in pyproject.toml [tool.uv]

packageRules.description: ffmpeg apt package resolves from the Ubuntu 24.04 (noble) universe archive, matching the GitHub runner's sources
igt-gpu-tools comes from Alpine edge (master branch of aports), not the 3.24-stable branch. The proxy tries main → community → testing under whichever branch we point at.
onevpl-intel-gpu comes from Alpine edge (master branch of aports), not the 3.24-stable branch.

Avoid duplicate PRs: the custom regex manager above already handles ghcr.io/home-assistant/* FROM lines in Dockerfiles; disabling the built-in dockerfile manager for those packages keeps the regex manager as the single source so we don't get two PRs (one per datasource) on every base-image bump. The /.../ matchPackageNames is regex syntax matching any package name containing 'home-assistant' — the dockerfile manager only sees image names, so this can only hit the HA base images.

Same duplicate-PR guard for docker-compose files: the custom regex manager above tracks the HA image tag in the dep-proxy e2e docker-compose.yml; the built-in docker-compose manager (enabled by ``config:recommended``) also parses ``image:`` lines by default, so without this rule an HA bump would open two competing PRs (one grouped, one not).

Hold CI Python on the 3.14 line to match the Alpine 3.24 base image runtime (python3=3.14.5-r0). minimumReleaseAge gives uv time to catch up: uv only installs interpreters embedded in its release, and [tool.uv] required-version is an exact pin, so a patch bump landing before uv ships support fails CI with no self-heal (cf. #409).

Override the helpers:pinGitHubActionDigestsToSemver preset's semver versioning for home-assistant/builder, which moved from semver tags (1.x-7.x) to calver tags (2026.06.0+). With semver versioning, the calver tags don't parse and Renovate proposes 'upgrades' to the old pre-calver semver tags (this surfaced as the bogus #246 and #248 PRs).

signalk/signalk-server publishes noisy rolling tags (latest-alpine, master-<major>-alpine, sha-<hash>-alpine, <major>-alpine) alongside its v<semver>-alpine releases. Restrict Renovate to the release tags so it tracks real versions and never proposes a rolling or bogus-major 'upgrade'.

Auto-merge rules below are order-dependent: renovate applies packageRules in array order and the last match wins. Deny anything that could reach a shipped artifact, so a future Dockerfile or runtime requirement defaults to manual review.

Actions here run in lint, test and release jobs that never produce an image. The container users install is built only on a release tag, by home-assistant/builder, which is carved out below and stays manual. The docker/build-push-action uses in the test workflows build throwaway images with load:true and never push, so they cannot reach a user either.
Lint and format tooling. Never shipped.
npm packages pinned in .pre-commit-config.yaml additional_dependencies. These come from the custom regex manager, which renovate names custom.regex, so the pre-commit rule above does not reach them.

Dev and test tooling only, scoped by depType: dependency-groups and tool.uv.dev-dependencies. Deliberately excludes project.dependencies, project.optional-dependencies and build-system.requires, so a runtime dependency added later defaults to manual review instead of inheriting auto-merge -- the pypi datasource is not in the denial above, so scoping here is the only guard. Repos that already ship runtime packages also deny them by name in the final rule. Only pep621 is listed because renovate has no separate uv manager: pep621 is the manager that handles uv projects, covering pyproject.toml, uv.lock and uv workspaces, so naming uv here would match nothing.

The uv required-version pin in [tool.uv], which comes from the custom regex manager rather than the native pep621 manager and so is not covered by the rule above. Scoped by depName so it does not sweep in the other custom.regex managers.
Majors always get a human. Must stay last to override every opt-in above.

MANUAL REVIEW: home-assistant/builder builds the container users install. Also broken out of the github-actions group so a builder bump does not block auto-merge of every other action riding in the same PR. Every other action here runs in jobs that never produce an image, so they auto-merge.
